record.paper_title: Methods for Computing All Roots of a Polynomial Simultaneously - Known Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Global convergence of a higher-order Weierstrass-type method
record.original_question: Fix the higher-order Weierstrass-type method (10), which has convergence rate R + 2. Is this method globally convergent outside a subset of C^n of measure zero? If so, describe the exceptional set; if not, determine where the conjectured global-convergence picture fails.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-\zeta_i)\in\mathbb{C}[z]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ with pairwise distinct (unknown) zeros $\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n\in\mathbb{C}$. For a vector $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n$ with pairwise distinct components, define the Weierstrass correction
$$W_i(x)=\frac{f(x_i)}{\prod_{j\ne i}(x_i-x_j)},\qquad i=1,\dots,n.$$
Fix an integer $R\ge 0$. Consider the higher-order Weierstrass-type iteration of convergence order $R+2$ defined componentwise by
$$x_i^{(k+1)} = x_i^{(k)} - W_i(x^{(k)})\sum_{r=0}^{R}\Bigg(\prod_{s=1}^{r}\sum_{\substack{j=1\\ j\ne i}}^{n}\frac{W_j(x^{(k)})}{x_i^{(k)}-x_j^{(k)}}\Bigg),\qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
where the empty product (case $r=0$) is interpreted as $1$. (For $R=0$ this reduces to the classical Weierstrass–Dochev method; increasing $R$ yields methods of increasing order $R+2$.)

Question: Is there a subset $E\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ of Lebesgue measure zero such that for every initial vector $x^{(0)}\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus E$ (with pairwise distinct components) the iteration is well-defined for all $k\ge 0$ and converges to a permutation of $(\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n)$? If yes, characterize the exceptional set $E$ explicitly; if not, identify the locus of initial conditions where the conjectured global convergence fails.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the higher-order Weierstrass-type method is globally convergent outside a measure-zero set in $\mathbb{C}^n$ is attributed to Kyurkchiev and Atanassova and has been studied in subsequent works on critical points and divergent starting configurations of these iterations. Available literature (papers on critical points of Kyurkchiev's method, divergent starting points, and recent local/semilocal convergence analyses) addresses partial aspects but does not establish global convergence almost everywhere. No proof of the full conjecture appears in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Critical Points of Kyurkchiev's Method for Solving Algebraic Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies critical points and divergent behavior of Kyurkchiev-type Weierstrass methods, addressing partial aspects of global convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on exceptional/critical starting points exist, but a full almost-everywhere global convergence theorem is not established.

status_evidence.title: Local and Semilocal Convergence of a Family of Multi-point Weierstrass-Type Root-Finding Methods
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2020) work proves only local/semilocal convergence results for Weierstrass-type families.
status_evidence.claim: Modern convergence results remain local or semilocal, not global a.e.

status_evidence.title: Convergence Analysis of a Modified Weierstrass Method
status_evidence.snippet: Provides convergence analysis under conditions on the initial approximation; does not prove global a.e. convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Global a.e. convergence of higher-order Weierstrass-type methods is not proved.
